exposure: Heart disease (Rheumatic Heart Disease, Congenital Heart Disease)
outcome: Maternal complications (pre-eclampsia, pulmonary oedema, cardiac failure mortality)
cohort: 100 pregnant women diagnosed with heart disease visiting a tertiary care centre in South India.
finding: Rheumatic heart disease was the most prevalent cardiac condition (55%) among pregnant women in this low-income setting, followed by congenital heart disease (26%).
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was the predominant mode of delivery (73%) among pregnant women with heart disease.
